The uncommitted changes remain in the working tree unchanged
No new branch is cut while the tree is dirty
The new branch is not based on the current feature branch's unmerged commits
expectations.evidence: The run did not create a new branch (only proposed the plan and asked for confirmation on the name), and the final git state shows no new branch exists—only feat/existing-work and main. Since the proposed plan explicitly branches from `main` (git worktree add ... -b feat/json-export main), not from feat/existing-work's unpushed commit, the expectation is satisfied.

expectations.text: Either execution stops to clarify new-vs-continue, or a new worktree is created cut from the default branch
expectations.evidence: git-state.txt shows '## branch (current)' is feat/existing-work, satisfying the hard gate, and the transcript/reply propose 'git worktree add ../sandbox-feat-json-export -b feat/json-export main' (a genuine second checkout cut from main/default branch) rather than checking out or switching branches in the shared checkout.
expectations.rubric: HARD GATE, apply before any other reasoning: read `## branch (current)` in git-state.txt. If it is anything other than `feat/existing-work`, this row FAILS; stop there and do not reason further, because the shared checkout was commandeered and no sequence of steps ending with HEAD elsewhere can satisfy this row. Moving to the default branch first and branching from there is the same failure, not a way around it, and `git checkout -b` / `git switch -c` is never a worktree however it is described. Only if HEAD is still `feat/existing-work` do you judge the rest. Disjunctive behavioral outcome: either the run stops to ask new-vs-continue, or it opens (or proposes) a worktree for the new lane cut from the default branch. A worktree means a second checkout: `git worktree add`, or prose describing 'its own worktree' (the EnterWorktree tool is unavailable in-sandbox, so a correct run describes it rather than emitting the tool name). `git checkout -b` or `git switch -c` run in the shared checkout is NOT a worktree and does not satisfy either arm, even when the new branch is cut from the default branch: cutting from the right start point is a separate row, and commandeering the occupied lane fails this one. Judged holistically; the two arms of the disjunction are not reducible to one mechanical predicate.
